use: About marriage, not dating: dokushin means not married.

example.romaji: ani wa mada dokushin da yo.
example.ja: 兄はまだ独身だよ。
example.english: My older brother's still single.

examplePolite.english: My older brother is still single.

use: Used casually for males of any age, and in school and sports for the boys' side.

example.romaji: danshi tte, honto kodomo da yo ne.
example.ja: 男子って、ほんと子供だよね。
example.english: Guys are such kids, right?

examplePolite.romaji: danshi tte hontou ni kodomo desu yo ne.
examplePolite.ja: 男子って本当に子供ですよね。
examplePolite.english: Guys really are like kids, aren't they?

use: A mid-level manager; also used like a name to address them.

example.romaji: kachou, kyou yasumi datte.
example.ja: 課長、今日休みだって。
example.english: Apparently the section chief is off today.

examplePolite.romaji: kachou wa kyou yasumi da sou desu.
examplePolite.ja: 課長は今日休みだそうです。
examplePolite.english: I hear the section chief is off today.

use: Casual and a bit rude; men also use it about themselves as a joke.

example.romaji: mou ossan da kara, tetsuya muri.
example.ja: もうおっさんだから、徹夜無理。
example.english: I'm an old man now, I can't pull all-nighters.

notes: The politer word is ojisan; for women, obasan.

example.romaji: ano futari, mukashi kara raibaru na n da.
example.ja: あの二人、昔からライバルなんだ。
example.english: Those two have been rivals forever.

examplePolite.romaji: ano futari wa mukashi kara raibaru desu.
examplePolite.ja: あの二人は昔からライバルです。
examplePolite.english: Those two have been rivals for a long time.

notes: Also for love rivals: koi no raibaru.

english: film director; team manager or coach
use: Also used like a name to address the director or coach.

example.romaji: ano eiga no kantoku, dare dattakke?
example.ja: あの映画の監督、誰だったっけ？
example.english: Who directed that movie again?

examplePolite.romaji: ano eiga no kantoku wa dare deshitakke?
examplePolite.ja: あの映画の監督は誰でしたっけ？
examplePolite.english: Who was the director of that movie again?

notes: As kantoku suru it means to supervise.

example.romaji: riidaa wa dare ga yaru?
example.ja: リーダーは誰がやる？
example.english: Who's going to be the leader?

examplePolite.romaji: riidaa wa dare ga yarimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: リーダーは誰がやりますか？

notes: Usually with yaru or naru: riidaa ni naru.

use: Often X no hou ga toshiue (X is older) or toshiue no hito (an older person).

example.romaji: kanojo, futatsu toshiue na n da.
example.ja: 彼女、二つ年上なんだ。
example.english: She's two years older than me.

examplePolite.english: She's two years older than me.

example.romaji: chuugakusei no toki, sakkaa yatteta.
example.ja: 中学生の時、サッカーやってた。
example.english: I played soccer in junior high.

examplePolite.romaji: chuugakusei no toki, sakkaa o yatte imashita.
examplePolite.ja: 中学生の時、サッカーをやっていました。
examplePolite.english: I played soccer in junior high.

example.romaji: imouto wa ima daigakusei da yo.
example.ja: 妹は今大学生だよ。
example.english: My little sister's in college now.

examplePolite.english: My younger sister is at university now.

use: Also works like an adjective: okanemochi da ne (you're rich).

example.romaji: kare no ie, sugoi okanemochi rashii yo.
example.ja: 彼の家、すごいお金持ちらしいよ。
example.english: Apparently his family's super rich.

examplePolite.romaji: kare no ie wa totemo okanemochi da sou desu.
examplePolite.ja: 彼の家はとてもお金持ちだそうです。
examplePolite.english: I hear his family is very rich.

use: Life as a whole story; daily routine is seikatsu.

example.romaji: jinsei de ichiban tanoshikatta.
example.ja: 人生で一番楽しかった。
example.english: That was the most fun I've had in my life.

examplePolite.ja: 人生で一番楽しかったです。
examplePolite.english: It was the most fun I've ever had.

notes: Not life as in being alive; that's inochi.

use: The current occasion, compared with past or future ones.

example.romaji: konkai wa watashi ga ogoru yo.
example.ja: 今回は私がおごるよ。
example.english: This time it's my treat.

examplePolite.ja: 今回は私がおごります。

notes: Last time is zenkai. kondo can mean this time but usually means next time.

use: Your everyday routine and how you get by.

example.romaji: kotchi no seikatsu, mou nareta?
example.ja: こっちの生活、もう慣れた？
example.english: Used to life here yet?

examplePolite.romaji: kochira no seikatsu ni wa mou naremashita ka?
examplePolite.ja: こちらの生活にはもう慣れましたか？
examplePolite.english: Have you gotten used to life here?

notes: Also seikatsu suru: to live, get by.

use: Also for periods of your own life: gakusei jidai (student days).

example.romaji: gakusei jidai wa okane nakatta naa.
example.ja: 学生時代はお金なかったなあ。
example.english: I had no money back in my student days.

examplePolite.romaji: gakusei jidai wa okane ga arimasen deshita.
examplePolite.ja: 学生時代はお金がありませんでした。
examplePolite.english: I didn't have any money in my student days.

notes: jidai ga chigau (times have changed) is a common line.

use: Follows a description: kodomo no koro (when I was a kid).

example.romaji: kodomo no koro, koko de yoku asondeta.
example.ja: 子供の頃、ここでよく遊んでた。
example.english: I used to play here a lot as a kid.

examplePolite.romaji: kodomo no koro, koko de yoku asonde imashita.
examplePolite.ja: 子供の頃、ここでよく遊んでいました。
examplePolite.english: I often played here when I was a child.

notes: After a clock time it becomes -goro: sanji goro (around three).

use: yotei ga aru = I have plans; after a verb it means you plan to do it.

example.romaji: shuumatsu, nanika yotei aru?
example.ja: 週末、何か予定ある？
example.english: Got any plans this weekend?

examplePolite.romaji: shuumatsu wa nanika yotei ga arimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 週末は何か予定がありますか？
examplePolite.english: Do you have any plans this weekend?

notes: ashita iku yotei = I'm planning to go tomorrow.

use: The formal word heard in shops, announcements and business; in chat say kyou.

example.romaji: honjitsu wa arigatou gozaimashita.
example.ja: 本日はありがとうございました。
example.english: Thank you for today.

use: A good opportunity, not a probability.

example.romaji: ima ga chansu da yo!
example.ja: 今がチャンスだよ！
example.english: Now's your chance!

example.romaji: mirai no koto nante wakannai yo.
example.ja: 未来のことなんてわかんないよ。
example.english: Nobody knows the future.

examplePolite.romaji: mirai no koto wa wakarimasen yo.
examplePolite.ja: 未来のことはわかりませんよ。
examplePolite.english: No one can know the future.

notes: Mix-up: your own future (career, plans) is usually shourai.
